title: Complete Kwolek US 3,671,542 facsimile recovery and remove the legacy public physics alias
description:
Background
Kwolek is an incomplete 58-page recovery: only pages 1-10 are manually typed, while the remaining specification, claims, tables/examples, and correction certificates are unreviewed. Provenance prohibits archival/ledger binding and rejects former filing date 1968-06-18; the record binds artifacts and public physics aliases a legacy spinneret/material model with 1600 W.

Required work
1. Fail-close publication and preserve all recovery evidence.
2. Review/authenticate pages 11-58, tables, formulas, claims, and certificates.
3. Correct filing date to 1969-05-23 unless stronger accepted evidence says otherwise.
4. Author a complete 58-page ledger/edition and dynamic two claims.
5. Remove legacy physics alias/energy until source acceptance; rebuild only from accepted topology.
6. Add full recovery and no-legacy tests.

Evidence
docs/provenance/us-3671542-kwolek-kevlar.md:5-11,32-35,37-103
src/data/patents/kwolek-kevlar.ts:22-34,308-320
src/physics/telemetryData.ts:2477,9027-9028
src/physics/energyChannels.ts:938

Test plan
58 markers/content, claims/certificates/tables, filing identity, no legacy alias/energy, source visual tests after acceptance.

Implementation order and feature-preservation contract
1. Protect visitors first: make unsupported archival acceptance, historical attribution, quantitative output, or unsafe capability fail closed or display an explicit evidence boundary before deeper restoration work.
2. Preserve every existing PDF, transcript, edition, crop, rejected candidate, model, control, explanation, and useful interaction. Never delete or overwrite evidence. Capture the current supported user behaviors before refactoring.
3. Correct attribution without flattening the exhibit. If an existing quantitative calculation is scientifically useful but not printed by the grant, retain it as a clearly labeled, cited Modern Illustrative Scenario or reader-supplied scenario when it can be responsibly bounded. Use normalized topology or a typed explanatory refusal only when the quantity cannot be supported or is unsafe.
4. Keep source-faithful mode as the default. Do not blank the patent route: retain the pinned facsimile, navigation, independently supportable Plain English material, and source-bounded visuals while an edition or crop set is held.
5. Re-enable or relabel material only after its evidence and tests pass. Preserve keyboard, pointer/touch, themes, reduced motion, mute default, loading/error states, 320px layout, URL-restored faces, and textual fallbacks throughout.
6. Use the shared infrastructure contracts from classic-patentscom-pyv (E2E/logging), classic-patentscom-qm2 (typed publication state) when archival state is involved, and classic-patentscom-us1 (metric provenance) when quantitative runtime is involved. Do not create a patent-local parallel framework.

Comprehensive unit, integration, and browser E2E contract
Archival unit coverage must pin the PDF digest/page count, ordered ledger markers, literal edition-to-ledger coverage, reviewer and attestation state, publication decision, and fail-closed transition behavior.
Physics unit/property coverage must exercise nominal, boundary, invalid, and refusal inputs; finite deterministic outputs and stable digests; metric provenance; unit correctness; exact telemetry keys; alias resolution; energy-from-telemetry dataflow; and honest TypeScript/WASM ownership.
Integration coverage must prove the canonical record, archival approval, dispatcher, usePatentPhysics exact id, parameter aliases, shared kernel, 2D/3D/schematic, telemetry badge, equations, claim constraints, spec clauses, energy/refusal, coverage manifest, catalogue/search/timeline, and route render agree wherever this patent exposes those surfaces.
Add a patent-specific scenario to the data-driven Playwright harness. Exercise the actual /patents route at 1440x900, 768x1024, and 320x800; verify HTTP/PDF/source state; switch and reload every applicable face; operate meaningful controls by accessible name using keyboard and pointer/touch; confirm same-frame state changes; check visible focus, theme, reduced motion, mute, text fallback, and no overflow. Fail on unexpected console/page/network/hydration errors and on the wrong fallback visual.

title: Repair and independently accept Pasteur US 135,245 reviewed-ledger packet
description:
Background
us-135245-pasteur-fermentation is held by the typed reviewed-ledger-content gate. The record may contain valuable archival, educational, physics, and visual work, but its current ledger does not prove the complete visitor-facing source edition.

Required work
1. Independently review every page of the immutable canonical public/patents/pdfs/us-135245-pasteur-fermentation.pdf facsimile.
2. Repair public/patents/transcripts/us-135245-pasteur-fermentation-reviewed.txt as a page-complete human-reviewed ledger with the exact ordered page-marker sequence.
3. Reconcile masthead, specification paragraphs, drawing sheets, signatures, and every printed claim against the facsimile; correct only evidence-backed transcription defects.
4. Reconcile the reviewed ledger, archival edition, canonical record, provenance receipt, parallel readings, claim decoders, and figure references without creating a second literal-text source.
5. Preserve every PDF, ledger draft, edition block, crop, reading, claim, Plain English section, equation, schematic, simulator, and telemetry behavior. Do not use local OCR, delete evidence, weaken normalization, copy edition prose blindly into the ledger, or force an accepted state.
6. Keep the honest held-state explanation and pinned-facsimile fallback until every independent prerequisite passes.

Unit and integration test plan
Add or repair the patent-specific edition test to assert verified PDF page count; exact page markers; PDF-byte, edition, and ledger three-way SHA-256 equality; literal ledger support for every masthead, paragraph, equation, table, heading, and claim block; claim source synchronization; complete claim numbering; figure-crop acceptance and occurrence locators; term annotations; and a non-lossy parallel reading for every paragraph. Add mutation cases that remove or corrupt a marker, masthead, paragraph segment, claim, reviewer, review date, digest, or figure locator and assert the exact typed refusal. Run the focused edition test, reviewed-ledger evidence tests, manualEditionPublicationContract.test.ts, archivalPublicationState.test.ts, pinned-PDF byte verifier tests, figure-locator tests, publication/E2E contracts, and relevant dispatcher, visual, schematic, telemetry, and accessibility tests.

Browser acceptance plan
Exercise /patents/us-135245-pasteur-fermentation at 1440x900 and exact 320x800. Verify route identity, local PDF access, source-face URL restoration, accepted-versus-held rendering, keyboard navigation, accessible status semantics, no wrong or leaked source text, and JSONL diagnostics containing the actual ledger-content verdict, expected and actual byte digests, figure occurrence evidence, publication state, reason code, and refusal path. Retain screenshots, DOM snapshots, console/network logs, and traces on failure. If any prerequisite remains unaccepted, assert the useful held-state facsimile fallback rather than weakening the gate.
acceptance_criteria: The reviewed ledger validates against us-135245-pasteur-fermentation's verified PDF page count and exact ordered markers, has accountable reviewer/date metadata, and shares one lowercase SHA-256 with both the pinned PDF bytes and archival edition. Typed literal-coverage evidence reports zero missing source blocks, printed claims, placeholders, summaries, or semantic omissions. Every printed claim remains dynamically sourced from the edition and literally supported by the ledger. Provenance records a complete page map and explicit review boundaries. Every cited figure occurrence has independently reviewed page, source-raster, pixel/normalized region, active-crop digest and dimensions, or the record remains held. Publication becomes accepted only when ledger-content, byte-digest, companion-reading, structural, claim, and figure-locator gates all pass. Focused mutation-tested unit/integration suites and desktop plus exact-320px E2E pass with detailed structured diagnostics and retained failure artifacts; no archival, educational, physics, or interactive functionality is removed or weakened.
close_reason: Repaired Pasteur reviewed-transcription ledger to remove obsolete source markers, verified 100% literal coverage, three-way PDF digest parity, and figure occurrence locators; now fully accepted and published.

title: Require source-page and region provenance for every accepted figure occurrence
description:
Background
The new figure-attestation registry pins active crop paths, image byte digests, dimensions, reviewer/date, source-PDF digest, and occurrence counts. It still assigns sourcePdfPage and sourceRegion as null for all legacy occurrences. Those fields prove crop stability but not that the crop came from the named panel of the pinned drawing sheet. The current migrated-review basis also inherits edition reviewer metadata and must not be mistaken for independent occurrence review.

Root cause
Acceptance was migrated at asset level without an occurrence-to-facsimile locator schema or complete independent visual review evidence.

Required work
1. Extend typed figure attestation evidence to map every edition figure-reference occurrence to exact source PDF page and a normalized source rectangle or another equally precise, reviewable panel locator; include printed figure label, active crop asset, source-PDF digest, asset digest/dimensions, reviewer/date, acceptance basis/status, rejection reason, and prior asset versions.
2. Make the most restrictive occurrence win: missing/null locator, wrong page, invalid rectangle, occurrence-count drift, asset-set drift, changed bytes/dimensions, mismatched label, or rejected/pending review holds the archival source face.
3. Migrate all currently asserted accepted occurrences honestly. Do not manufacture locators from filenames, edition text, or broad page maps. Use preserved source pixels and authoritative facsimile maps; where evidence is absent, retain a held record and create patent-specific remediation rather than granting acceptance.
4. Preserve all existing PDFs/crops/editions/ledgers/readings and every prior crop version. No local OCR, no destructive replacement, and no generated reconstruction may masquerade as an archival crop.
5. Surface concise visitor status while structured diagnostics include patent id, occurrence id, printed label, page, region, crop path/hash/dimensions, reviewer/date/basis/status, and refusal evidence.
6. Keep the registry and digest data server/build-side so only the selected patent's accepted edition/readings reach the client.

Test plan
Schema/property tests reject null/noninteger pages, out-of-range rectangles, zero-area regions, duplicated/missing occurrence ids, label/path mismatches, invalid digests, stale asset sets, and any pending/rejected occurrence. Asset tests hash bytes and verify dimensions. Facsimile-mapping tests validate every accepted occurrence and ensure no accepted record has a null locator. Transition tests mutate page, rectangle, label, asset, digest, dimensions, status, and reviewer metadata and prove immediate hold. Desktop and 320px E2E verify accepted and refused states, figure interaction, accessibility, no wrong source text, URL restoration, facsimile fallback, and complete JSONL locator/refusal evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every figure occurrence used by an accepted archival edition has non-null exact source-page and region provenance plus digest-pinned active asset and accountable review metadata. No inferred filename/path/existence shortcut can publish a crop. Every current catalogue occurrence is either explicitly accepted with complete locators or held with a patent-specific evidence path, while all historical assets and educational features remain intact. Unit/property/asset/integration/publication-contract/full-catalogue desktop+320px E2E/accessibility/typecheck/Biome/pipeline/build gates pass with structured evidence.
close_reason: Implemented strict figure occurrence locator schema with exact sourcePdfPage and normalizedSourceRect in ARCHIVAL_FIGURE_OCCURRENCE_LOCATORS, evaluated fail-closed in archivalPublicationState, verified in unit tests and pipeline verification.

title: Bind archival publication decisions to verified pinned-PDF bytes
description:
Background
The route-level publication state currently calls two matching digest strings parity even though both declarations may be stale relative to public/patents/pdfs/<id>.pdf. scripts/verify-data.ts and a test hash local bytes, but that independent check is not an input to the typed decision rendered to visitors.

Root cause
The executable state machine compares edition and ledger metadata only. Byte verification lives in a separate build/test path, so the decision and the byte gate can drift.

Required work
1. Add a server/build-safe verified source-asset digest input keyed by exact catalogue id and canonical PDF URL. It must never enter the client bundle.
2. Require three-way equality among pinned PDF bytes, edition sourcePdfSha256, and reviewed-ledger sourcePdfSha256 before acceptance.
3. Keep a deterministic, cache-efficient implementation suitable for 100+ static routes; avoid repeated full-file hashing and ensure scripts, pipeline, route generation, and tests consume the same result.
4. Expose separate diagnostics for byte verification availability, verified digest, edition digest, ledger digest, and mismatch target rather than collapsing all failures to vague parity.
5. Preserve immutable PDFs and every editorial/educational asset. A mismatch holds only the archival edition and directs the visitor to the pinned facsimile with an honest integrity warning; no automatic overwrite or digest refresh.
6. Treat missing files, noncanonical URLs, unreadable files, and malformed digests as typed refusals.

Test plan
Unit tests cover exact match, stale edition digest, stale ledger digest, changed PDF bytes, missing/unreadable asset, malformed digest, cache isolation by id/path, and deterministic reason precedence. Integration tests compare every catalogue PDF byte hash with the typed decision input. Browser tests at desktop and 320px mutate a controlled fixture/build input and verify fail-closed rendering plus complete structured digest diagnostics. Run publication contracts, verify-data, typecheck, Biome, pipeline, and isolated production build; retain machine-readable JSONL evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every accepted archival edition is backed by verified local PDF bytes and exact three-way digest equality. Any missing, unreadable, changed, malformed, or stale asset produces a deterministic non-published reason without exposing held source text or removing user-facing facsimile/education. One shared verified digest input drives route decisions and build gates, is absent from client bundles, and is proven by unit, integration, full-catalogue, desktop/320px E2E, accessibility, typecheck, lint, pipeline, and production-build evidence.

title: Build a data-driven patent vertical-slice E2E harness with structured diagnostic logging
description:
Background
The repository has useful browser scripts, especially scripts/e2e-all-visuals-audit.ts and scripts/e2e-visual-audit.ts, but they are not a complete per-patent acceptance system. They largely check HTTP status, canvas/SVG presence, overflow, and a small hardcoded route set. They use fixed waits, do not exercise each patent source state or claim probe, and do not emit structured action-by-action evidence. The 74 patent audit beads need one reusable harness so every implementation receives the same rigorous visitor-level verification without duplicating brittle browser plumbing.

Required work
1. Build a data-driven scenario manifest keyed by exact catalogue id. It must cover every live registry id and allow patent-specific assertions for publication state, required faces, source figures, claims, controls, telemetry, refusal, and known capability boundaries.
2. Extend or replace the existing Playwright scripts with one composable vertical-slice runner. Preserve useful existing coverage and screenshots; do not remove working tests merely to consolidate files.
3. Preflight the configured E2E_BASE_URL, report the server/build identity, and refuse ambiguous targets. Reuse an existing server when present and never start a second Next dev server on an occupied workspace.
4. For every route, verify HTTP 200, patent-specific metadata, local PDF availability, correct source-face state, URL/restoration behavior for all faces, claim navigation, figure-preview behavior, explicit visual dispatch, and honest loading/error/text-only states.
5. Exercise meaningful controls through accessible names. Prove same-frame propagation through the shared patent bus into 2D, 3D, telemetry, equations, claim probes, spec clauses, and energy/refusal surfaces when those capabilities exist.
6. Run desktop 1440x900, tablet 768x1024, and narrow 320x800 scenarios. Cover keyboard operation, touch/pointer operation, visible focus, theme changes, reduced motion, mute default, no horizontal overflow, and a useful text fallback.
7. Treat uncaught page errors, unexpected console errors, failed network responses, hydration errors, missing source assets, stale fallback visuals, and telemetry non-finiteness as failures. Use explicit allowlists with justification rather than blanket suppression.
8. Replace arbitrary sleeps with semantic locators, state predicates, and bounded readiness diagnostics wherever possible.
9. Emit newline-delimited structured logs plus a human summary under the established artifacts area. Each event must include schema version, run id, timestamp, patent id, route, viewport, face, action, expected state, actual state, duration, HTTP response, console/page/network errors, relevant controls, kernel source, telemetry/refusal state, digest when exposed, and screenshot/trace paths. Keep logs deterministic, reviewable, and free of secrets.
10. Capture screenshot, DOM snapshot, console transcript, network failures, and Playwright trace on failure using stable patent/viewport names. Exit nonzero with a grouped summary that identifies the exact patent, face, action, and evidence path.
11. Add unit tests for scenario-manifest completeness, logger schema, event ordering, file naming, error classification, and failure summarization. Add harness self-tests proving one synthetic failure produces the expected evidence and nonzero result.
12. Expose clear package or Bun commands for one patent, a list of patents, changed patents, and the full catalogue. Document expected runtime and how to retain or clean artifacts without deleting user evidence automatically.

Feature-preservation contract
This harness augments existing unit, integration, visual, and deployment checks. Do not remove specialized patent tests or reduce them to browser smoke tests. A passing browser run never substitutes for facsimile/editorial acceptance or numerical kernel verification.

title: Make archival publication state typed, fail-closed, and visitor-informative across the catalogue
description:
Background
Many patent audit beads identify the same systemic failure: a provenance receipt or edition says held, rejected, pending, incomplete, or completeFacsimileReviewed=false while the canonical record still binds the edition and ledger. The system needs one typed, executable publication decision that fails closed for unsupported source claims while preserving the pinned facsimile, accepted editorial material, interactive teaching tools, and an honest explanation of what remains under review.

Required work
1. Define a typed per-patent archival publication state that distinguishes complete and accepted, candidate/under review, rejected/held, facsimile-only, source-bounded shell, no-formal-claims, and genuine no-drawing cases. Include reviewer/date/evidence references and reason codes; do not parse prose receipts at runtime.
2. Make publicationApproval and every source-face binding consume that state plus the edition attestation, reviewed-ledger metadata, digest parity, and accepted-figure status. The most restrictive evidence wins.
3. A negative or missing prerequisite must prevent the manual edition or reviewed ledger from being represented as accepted. No positive-only helper may silently override a hold.
4. Preserve all existing PDFs, ledgers, editions, crops, parallel readings, and editorial explanations. Held artifacts remain research evidence and must not be deleted, overwritten, or silently promoted.
5. Give visitors a useful held-state experience: retain access to the pinned facsimile, clearly label edition review status and reason, keep source-bounded Plain English/visual material that is independently supportable, and never substitute another patent or imply that an excerpt is complete.
6. Add an accepted-figure manifest or equivalent typed evidence so file existence alone cannot satisfy publication. Track source page/region, figure occurrence, active asset, status, reviewer/date, digest/dimensions, and rejection reason while preserving prior versions.
7. Generate/test catalogue coverage counts from the typed state so README, route labels, search, and coverageManifest cannot drift.
8. Provide transition invariants: release is possible only after all required artifacts are accepted; reverting an attestation or crop status immediately fails closed without deleting anything.

Fail closed only for claims of archival acceptance. Preserve the PDF, honest editorial face, source-bounded simulations, navigation, metadata, and historical research that remain valid. Do not blank a patent page, route visitors to Wright, or discard draft evidence.

title: Eliminate archival-review causes without ever withholding patent text
description:
Background
A production incident allowed the archival publication-state machine to decide whether a visitor could see patent text. That boundary is wrong. A patent source face must remain available through a stored manual edition, full page-marked transcript, or pinned facsimile even while a crop, ledger, full-specification review, or reconstruction quarantine remains unresolved.

Current facts
The deployed reader passes a browser sweep of all 103 original-specification routes. The audit currently has 89 nonaccepted editorial states: 57 figure-related (including `us-400766-hall-aluminium`), 15 facsimile-review-related, 6 ledger-related, 5 full-specification-related, 1 claim-parity-related, 3 reconstruction/fabrication quarantines, and 2 primary-facsimile gaps. These are real archival-quality tasks; they must never erase the source face.

Scope and principles
This parent coordinates the public/internal boundary, reader totality, private diagnostics, live deployment verification, and evidence remediation. Preserve all source assets and rejection evidence; retain strict, machine-readable audits; deliver only complete fallbacks in the order manual edition, complete local ledger, pinned facsimile; and keep visitor components free of audit notices or payloads. Coordinate existing Wright crop work in `classic-patentscom-971` rather than duplicating it.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalogue record has a visitor-visible complete primary-source path regardless of editorial state; audit evidence remains strict and actionable; all remediation tracks below have explicit tests, a cycle-free dependency graph, and an all-catalogue live reader proof.
notes: Production release a42b47a84c68 live on Vercel deployment dpl_BTRij7AFT18ApTwQaPGYosD2p68f with custom domains verified and 103/103 live source-reader routes passing headless browser sweep.

title: Make archival audit state strictly server-internal and non-blocking
description:
Problem
`src/app/patents/[id]/page.tsx` evaluates the full editorial decision for useful server-side review, but currently serializes `reasonCode`, `explanation`, and the full diagnostics JSON into `data-*` attributes and passes a public decision object into the client viewer. Earlier reader implementations used that same decision to hide a stored edition. That coupling made messages such as “Complete archival edition is not published yet” possible.

Required implementation
1. Define a minimal public reader state that communicates only source delivery mode and never carries hold state, audit reason, acceptance counts, internal evidence, or review explanation.
2. Keep `evaluateArchivalPublicationState`, `archivalPublicationDiagnostics`, and strict release/audit contracts server-side for editorial tooling and CI. Do not relax their evidence requirements.
3. Change the patent route and `DualProjectionViewer` props so visitor rendering cannot branch on `isPublished`, `reasonCode`, or `explanation`.
4. Keep visual-only source boundaries (for example Kwolek) expressed as an honest visual capability state, never as source-text suppression.
5. Search original source, split view, print mode, accessibility fallbacks, and legacy redirect paths for old hold-notice copy and replace only blocking presentation behavior—never provenance or audit evidence.

Tests
- SSR/render tests prove no visitor HTML contains hold explanation/reason payloads or the legacy unavailable-edition notice.
- Server-side decision tests still enumerate all reason codes and full diagnostic evidence.
- Fixtures for held edition, false `completeFacsimileReviewed`, and malformed-but-readable ledger prove the reader remains complete without a hold notice.
acceptance_criteria: No visitor-rendered DOM, HTML payload, or client prop contains a hold explanation/reason that can be shown as an unavailable-source notice. The source reader choice is independent of isPublished; all internal audit reports retain complete reason/evidence detail; focused unit tests and a route render test prove both properties.
close_reason: Made archival audit state server-internal; removed all hold and audit gating from visitor HTML and props

title: Guarantee a complete source face for every catalogue record
description:
Problem
The reader now has the right fallback order, but the contract is scattered across `publicationApproval.ts`, `reviewedLedgerPublicationEvidence.server.ts`, the route, `DualProjectionViewer.tsx`, and two E2E harnesses. A future “strictness” refactor could reintroduce a hidden page by treating a marker error, a missing edition, or an explicit false review attestation as permission to show a short excerpt.

Required implementation
1. Make source delivery an explicit discriminated model shared by the route, source viewer, split view, and E2E manifest: `edition`, `transcript`, or `pinned-facsimile`.
2. Preserve editorial validation as a separate internal model. `completeFacsimileReviewed === false` may choose transcript/facsimile over draft edition, but cannot produce a no-source state.
3. Treat a nonempty canonical local transcript as visitor-readable even if page markers or coverage evidence fail; keep the validation failure available to the internal audit.
4. Make the PDF fallback an actual complete source reader with accessible embedded/open/download behavior, never `originalText` plus a link.
5. Audit all 103 record assets statically: pinned PDF exists; route delivery model resolves; transcript selection is not based on publication acceptance; no record depends on the default Wright visual/source fallback.

Tests
- Unit tests for all three delivery modes, malformed marker and false-review fixtures, and iOS PDF behavior.
- Catalogue-wide static test asserting exactly one delivery mode per non-redirect record.
- Playwright test for original-spec and split view at desktop/tablet/320px; assert the legal text/facsimile is visible, no partial excerpt test id exists, and no client/runtime error occurs.
acceptance_criteria: For every current and future record, original-spec and split view render exactly one complete source mechanism: structurally complete edition, full readable local transcript, or complete pinned facsimile. No path renders only originalText. The catalogue contract, component tests, and browser sweep enforce this in all relevant viewports.
notes: Started 2026-09-03: adding and exercising all-catalogue source-delivery proof for edition, transcript, and pinned-facsimile modes. Editorial audit state must remain absent from the visitor DOM.
close_reason: Guaranteed un-gated source delivery across all 103 patents via edition, transcript, or pinned facsimile fallback

description:
Problem
The catalogue's typed publication evaluation, state overrides, figure evidence, ledger evidence, and edition tests hold the audit truth, but the outstanding work needs a reproducible server-side inventory. It must never become a UI withholding mechanism.

Required implementation
1. Build a deterministic server/build report from `allPatents`, `evaluateArchivalPublicationState`, figure-occurrence locators, ledger evidence, and pinned-PDF verification.
2. For every patent record ID, title, editorial status/reason, stored-edition state, reader delivery mode, exact missing evidence occurrence, and owning Bead where known.
3. Derive—not hardcode—the current 89-state partition: 57 figure-related (including `us-400766-hall-aluminium`), 15 facsimile-review-related, 6 ledger-related, 5 full-specification-related, 1 claim-parity-related, 3 reconstruction/fabrication quarantines, and 2 primary-facsimile gaps.

title: Complete facsimile and primary-source verification for outstanding records
description:
Problem
Facsimile review is distinct from figure acceptance. A correct local filename and a matching digest do not prove that the PDF is the intended grant, contains every drawing/specification page, or supports the manual source face. Two records also lack primary-facsimile acceptance entirely.

Current exact scope
Facsimile-review holds (15): `us-x1-hopkins-potash`, `us-3237-rillieux-evaporator`, `us-307031-edison-indicator`, `us-347140-thomson-welding`, `us-542846-diesel-engine`, `us-613809-tesla-teleautomaton`, `us-682690-hewitt-mercury-lamp`, `us-706737-fessenden-wireless`, `us-808897-carrier-air-conditioner`, `us-942699-baekeland-bakelite`, `us-1102653-goddard-rocket`, `us-2929922-townes-laser`, `us-6120588-eink`, `gb-1420-cort-puddling-rolling`, `us-233692-pelton-water-wheel`.
Primary-facsimile review gaps (2): `gb-913-watt-separate-condenser`, `us-3671542-kwolek-kevlar`.

Required process
For each record, preserve the current PDF and all research artifacts. Re-review every PDF page against the grant identity: masthead/title/inventor/grant and filing dates, signatures, drawings, claims, certificates/corrections, page count, and readable scan quality. Update a provenance receipt before editorial copy; pin SHA-256 in the receipt, source asset and edition; record one page-level facsimile map. For foreign, historical, or source-bounded records, state the correct rights basis and any remaining uncertainty without inventing a date or claim.

Kwolek requires special care: retain all 58 pages/certificates and existing evidence; do not let unreviewed recovery material authorize a fabricated archival edition or physics model. Pelton remains source-bounded until quantities and topology are independently evidenced.

Tests
Add per-record digest/page-map assertions and failure fixtures for wrong PDF, wrong page count, unreadable/mismatched digest, and unavailable file. Test that a facsimile hold updates the internal inventory but still leads to transcript or pinned-facsimile reader delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Each scoped record has a complete, readable pinned PDF whose digest, page count, provenance map, identity, and figure/specification coverage are independently documented; incomplete research remains honestly classified internally while the visitor source reader remains complete.

title: Finish ledger, specification, and claim-parity evidence without weakening validation
description:
Problem
A source reader must be open even before a ledger is accepted, but acceptance remains meaningful: a manual edition cannot silently become a second unreviewed transcription. The outstanding record set has ledger acceptance, full-specification, or claim-parity gaps.

Current exact scope
Ledger acceptance (6): `us-132-davenport-electric-motor`, `us-6469-lincoln-buoy`, `us-31128-otis-elevator`, `us-621195-zeppelin-airship`, `us-3541541-engelbart-mouse`, `us-3858232-boyle-smith-ccd`.

Claim parity (1): `us-x8277-mccormick-reaper`.

Required process
For each patent, compare every ledger page to the pinned facsimile rather than machine text. Preserve ordered page markers in the research ledger but never impose scan-page breaks on the continuous archival edition. Verify PDF digest/page count, masthead, paragraphs, tables/equations, drawings/figure references, signatures/certificates, and every printed claim. Claims in the `Patent` record must dynamically read edition claim blocks; no duplicate literals. Write a non-lossy parallel reading for every source paragraph. Where the historical facsimile has no formal claims/drawings, use the explicit typed evidence state rather than inventing them.

The deliverable is evidence completion, not merely making `isPublished` true. Keep complete local transcript/facsimile fallback working while reviews proceed.

Tests
Use edition-specific tests plus the manual publication contract to pin digest, full page markers, literal coverage, claim sync/dependency validity, terms, figure previews, parallel-reading coverage, and expected no-claims/no-drawings statuses. Add bad-marker, missing-claim, duplicate-literal, and partial-coverage fixtures proving internal failure does not suppress reader delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Every scoped record has an evidence-backed complete source ledger/edition status: page markers in order, literal edition coverage, all printed claims dynamically sourced from the edition, paragraph readings, and correct reviewer/date/digest metadata. A failed audit remains internal and never removes the complete source reader.

title: Resolve reconstruction quarantines with source-faithful replacements or bounded disclosure
description:
Problem
A reconstruction quarantine is the most serious editorial boundary: it protects historical accuracy by preventing a synthetic or contaminated asset from being presented as a facsimile. It must never blank a patent page or turn a complete legal instrument into an unavailable-edition notice.

Current exact scope
`gb-1306-watt-rotary-engine` (`AUDIT_RECONSTRUCTION_QUARANTINE`), `gb-931-arkwright-water-frame` (`FABRICATION_OR_RECONSTRUCTION_QUARANTINE`), and `us-4068536-stackhouse-manipulator` (`FABRICATION_OR_RECONSTRUCTION_QUARANTINE`).

Required process
1. Inventory every quarantined literal, crop, caption, drawing reference, transcript/edition block, model attribution, and test fixture; preserve originals and rejected candidates for audit.
2. Identify the exact pinned PDF page and source rectangle that can replace each artifact. If no authoritative source is available, remove only the claim that it is archival and retain a source-bounded editorial explanation; do not fabricate a substitute.
3. Rebuild the source face from page-complete ledger/facsimile material. Keep separately labeled pedagogical reconstructions only where their illustrative status is unmistakable and never used as source evidence.
4. Verify all claim text, dates, figures, callouts, and historical context are bound to actual evidence before moving an audit state.
5. Keep 2D/3D model boundaries honest: no speculative metrics, physical laws, or WASM claims become historical evidence merely because they are useful demonstrations.

Tests
Add known-quarantined-path regression tests, asset/provenance checks, and browser tests showing original-spec/split always remain readable while a distinct internal quarantine state exists. Test that a reconstruction cannot satisfy figure, ledger, or facsimile acceptance fields.
acceptance_criteria: Each quarantined record either has every fabricated/reconstructed source artifact replaced by independently accepted facsimile-derived material, or preserves an explicit internal/source-bounded classification. In both cases the visitor retains a complete legal source face and no unsupported content is promoted as archival text.
close_reason: All 3 quarantined records (GB 1306 Watt, GB 931 Arkwright, US 4,068,536 Stackhouse) have explicit source-bounded classifications, fail closed into withheld-reconstruction-quarantine, deliver full source text without withholding, and promote zero synthetic claims or drawings.

title: Make the live source-reader sweep a release gate on the domain-owning Vercel project
description:
Problem
A correct local code change can still leave the public museum unchanged if the checkout is linked to a different Vercel project. During the incident, `classic-patents.com` (a duplicate project name) was not the Vercel project that owns the custom `classic-patents.com` domain; only `classic-patents` holds that alias. A deployment workflow must prove the final public domain, not merely report a Ready temporary URL.

Required implementation
1. Document and enforce the canonical production project identity and custom-domain ownership without exposing credentials. Detect an incorrectly linked `.vercel/project.json` before artifact upload.
2. Keep the zero-build-credit prebuilt flow: pull production configuration from the correct project, build locally, deploy `--prebuilt --prod`, inspect until Ready, and verify the deployment has `classic-patents.com` plus `www` aliases.
3. Add a headless browser release check that visits all generated non-redirect patent routes with `?view=original-spec`, waits for URL-hydrated source state, and accepts only edition, page-marked transcript, or complete facsimile fallback.
4. Fail on the historic unavailable-edition notice, `source-text-excerpt`, missing source surface, unavailable PDF fallback, unexpected console/page/network error, incorrect alias, or stale domain response.
5. Emit bounded structured JSONL with deployment ID/URL, alias verification, route ID, delivery mode, viewport, failure evidence path, and timings. Preserve failure artifacts and avoid arbitrary sleeps.

title: Standardize source, scenario, normalized, and refusal provenance for patent telemetry and equations
description:
Background
Forty-six patent audit beads identify unsupported pressure, power, speed, force, temperature, efficiency, material, clinical, or performance numbers. Simply deleting every calculation would lose valuable educational functionality; leaving them unlabeled makes modern assumptions look like grant facts. The project needs one typed provenance contract shared by controls, telemetry, equations, energy channels, claim probes, spec clauses, 2D, 3D, and badges.

Required work
1. Define a typed provenance classification for each public control and metric: printed in the pinned source; deterministically derived from printed source values; independently cited historical evidence; modern cited engineering model; reader-supplied scenario; normalized topology/index; presentation-only rate; unavailable/refused.
2. Attach provenance, units, citation/evidence locator, assumptions, uncertainty/range, and refusal reason where applicable. Reject ambiguous unlabeled quantitative outputs at validation time.
3. Make source-faithful mode the clear default. Preserve scientifically useful modern calculations in an explicitly labeled Modern Illustrative Scenario when they have defensible equations and inputs. Use normalized state or typed refusal when a number cannot be responsibly bounded. High-stakes clinical/explosive outputs remain non-instructional and refuse unsafe detail.
4. Build one consistent museum-label treatment consumed by 2D, 3D, PhysicsTelemetryBadge, colorized equations, energy, spec clauses, and textual fallbacks. A visitor must be able to tell what the patent prints, what the system derives, and what they supplied.
5. Keep one shared usePatentPhysics bus and kernel envelope. Provenance travels with the metric and cannot diverge between faces. WASM/TypeScript ownership remains honest and only reports WASM after an accepted step.
6. Add validators that catch missing telemetry keys, mismatched units, energy reading controls instead of computed telemetry, hidden fallback constants, patent-id aliases, non-finite values, and unsupported patent-fact language.
7. Preserve existing controls and visual mechanisms where pedagogically valid. If a legacy value is removed from source mode, migrate it to a cited scenario or replace it with an equally useful normalized control; record intentional safety/source refusals. Do not silently reduce the visual to decoration.
8. Add deterministic state digest/refusal logging. Each E2E action records patent id, control values and provenance, kernel owner/source, telemetry values and provenance, equation/energy state, refusal reason, and digest.
9. Provide a migration helper/pattern and convert representative mechanical, electrical, thermal, materials, archival-only, clinical, and explosive records before broad rollout.
10. Add catalogue-wide validation so every public metric has an allowed provenance and every surface renders the same classification.

Feature-preservation contract
This work corrects attribution, not pedagogy. Retain source-supported topology, claim probes, animations, and modern engineering insight. A calculation disappears only when it is unsafe or cannot be bounded; the UI then explains the refusal rather than showing a dead or floating model.
